2026-11-04.note: Hockey Academy night 6:15–7:45pm (The Lindum). One pan, about 20 minutes.

ingredients: 300g raw king prawns (frozen is fine, defrosted)
300g cherry tomatoes, halved (or a 400g tin chopped tomatoes)
2 tbsp cream cheese, or a splash of cream
Grated parmesan, and a squeeze of lemon if you have one, to serve
steps: Soften the onion in the oil in a wide pan for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the orzo and tomatoes and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until the orzo is almost tender. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the prawns and cook for 3–4 minutes until they're pink all the way through.
Stir in the cream cheese and spinach until the spinach wilts. Season.
Serve with parmesan and a squeeze of lemon.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: scoop hers out before the lemon and cut the prawns into small pieces. Defrost frozen prawns in the fridge from the morning, or in a bowl of cold water for 20 minutes.

2026-11-05.note: Bonfire night, out to watch the fireworks. A chippy tea as a treat, no cooking.

2026-11-06.meal: Garlic butter baked haddock with crushed new potatoes & peas
2026-11-06.note: Normal evening — gymnastics & swimming done earlier today, nothing on for tea

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the new potatoes for 15–18 minutes until tender.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and a squeeze of lemon. Put the haddock on a lined tray and brush over the butter.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Cook the peas for the last 4 minutes of the potatoes.
Drain and lightly crush the potatoes with a fork, stir through the parsley and a knob of butter.
Serve the fish with the crushed potatoes, peas and lemon wedges.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: leave the garlic butter off her portion and check carefully for bones.

2026-11-07.meal: Butternut squash, chickpea & spinach curry (double batch)
2026-11-07.note: Free evening after this morning's hockey match & Jess's me-time — good day to batch-cook extra for Wednesday's Hockey Academy Night

ingredients: 1 large butternut squash (about 1kg), peeled and diced
steps: Soften the onions in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin and turmeric and cook for 1 minute.
Add the squash, chickpeas, chopped tomatoes and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 20–25 minutes, until the squash is tender.
Take out Mathilda's portion and the 4 portions to freeze, keeping both mild.
Stir the spinach through the rest and cook for 3–4 minutes until wilted. Season.
Cook the rice and serve with the curry.
Cool the 4 extra portions within an hour, then portion into labelled containers (contents + today's date) and freeze flat for the meal drawer.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers plain with no extra pepper, and mash the squash a little finer. On Monday evening, move the frozen portions to the fridge so they're defrosted in time for Wednesday's reheat.

2026-11-08.meal: Slow-cooker gammon with parsley sauce, mash & peas
2026-11-08.note: This week's one meat night. Francis's away hockey fixture today — time still TBC, so slow cooker on before you set off and tea's ready whenever you're back. Alex's last day before CYCLONE starts tomorrow.

ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (or 1 tbsp dried)
steps: Put the gammon, onion and bay leaves in the slow cooker and pour over the water or stock.
Cover and cook on low for 5–6 hours, until the gammon is tender and shreds easily.
Lift out the gammon, rest for 5 minutes, then slice or shred, discarding any string and excess fat.
For the sauce, melt the butter in a pan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until thickened, then stir in the parsley.
Boil and mash the potatoes. Cook the peas for 4–5 minutes.
Serve the gammon with mash, peas and parsley sauce.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: rinse her portion briefly if the gammon's salty, and go light on the sauce. On by 9am so it's ready whenever you're back from the fixture.

2026-11-09.meal: Sweet potato & spinach dhal with rice (double batch)
2026-11-09.note: Mathilda's hospital eye test this morning (off nursery) — a quiet one at home for the rest of the day, so a good evening to batch-cook extra for tomorrow's Hull hockey training. Alex now away for CYCLONE.

steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, lentils and stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils and sweet potato are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and spinach and cook for 3–4 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Take out Mathilda's portion and 4 portions to cool for Tuesday before seasoning the rest.
Cook the rice and serve with the dhal.
Cool the 4 extra portions within an hour, cover and keep in the fridge for Tuesday (no need to freeze).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers plain and mash the sweet potato a little finer.

2026-11-10.meal: Reheat: Monday's sweet potato & spinach dhal with rice
2026-11-10.note: Hull hockey training 6–7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — tea ready for whoever's not driving, kept warm for the rest

ingredients: 4 portions of Monday's dhal (from the fridge)
steps: Tip the dhal into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8–10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4–5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the rice while the dhal heats.
Serve straightaway.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through before serving. Anyone back late from training can have theirs microwaved separately.

2026-11-11.meal: Reheat: Saturday's butternut squash curry (from the freezer)
2026-11-11.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15–7:45pm (The Lindum) — Saturday's frozen curry portions, moved to the fridge on Monday night, make a quick reheat either side of the run

ingredients: 4 portions of Saturday's butternut squash curry (defrosted in the fridge since Monday)
steps: Tip the curry into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8–10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 5–6 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the rice while the curry heats.
Serve straightaway.
recipe.tip: It's been frozen, so check extra carefully that it's piping hot all the way through, and only reheat it once.

2026-11-12.note: Mathilda's Scotter Primary open day this morning — evening's free, nothing on for tea

ingredients: Zest of 1 lemon, plus a squeeze of juice
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Cook the pasta according to the pack instructions, then drain, saving a mugful of the water.
Season the salmon and pan-fry for 3–4 minutes each side until just cooked through, then flake into chunks.
In a separate pan, soften the leek in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the peas and a splash of the pasta water, and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the crème fraîche and lemon zest, and warm through. Take out Mathilda's portion of sauce now if she's sensitive to lemon.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice to the rest, then toss the pasta through the sauce with the flaked salmon.
Serve with a sprinkle of cheese.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: flake her salmon extra small and check carefully for bones.
